messages:
maria: Heads up — we need a design for SLO-driven routing that ties customer tier + region to model-variant fallbacks. Short sync?
kevin: +1. Are we thinking circuit-breakers per-tenant or per-route?
raj: leaning per-tenant with per-route overrides. Tenants have different p99 targets, quotas, and SLAs.
kevin: ok, but circuit-breaker signal: error rate alone misses latency spikes. propose hybrid: p95 latency breach OR error rate > X over window.
sophie: Agreed. Also need to consider queued requests/backpressure. If queue depth grows, fallback earlier to cheaper model variant.
maria: Good point. We should define thresholds: e.g., Gold: p99 < 300ms, availability >= 99.9%; Silver: p99 < 700ms, availability >= 99.5%. If breach then try fallback chain.
olivia: For the fallback chain, recommended variants: full model -> quantized-8bit -> distil variant. Want automated auto-fallback plus manual override in Console.
kevin: How do we represent policy? Draft DSL idea:
```yaml
policy:
  tiers:
    gold:
      p99_latency_ms: 300
      availability: 0.999
      fallback: ["model-xl-q8", "model-large-q4"]
      cb_window_s: 60
      cb_threshold: 0.03  # fraction of requests failing SLO in window
    silver:
      p99_latency_ms: 700
      availability: 0.995
      fallback: ["model-large-q4"]
```
maria: Nice. Need to define metric naming so Console and API align: e.g., routing.slo.p99_ms, routing.slo.breach_rate, routing.cb.state.
raj: Telemetry: expose per-tenant heatmap in Console showing p50/p95/p99, breach_count, cb_state, and estimated cost delta if fallback triggered.
kevin: UX: small slider to tune cb_threshold per-tenant and a 'preview' mode that simulates decisions on recent telemetry. No hard rollout until ops confirms.
sophie: API semantics: POST /route/evaluate should return {decision: "route|fallback|reject", reason, chosen_model, telemetry_snapshot}. Keep it idempotent and cheap.
maria: Rollout plan: start internal-only with 2 tenants for 48h, capture regressions via evals. Add canary flag for automatic fallback on deploys.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy for routing-operator v0.9 started (canary: 2 hosts) — watch routing.cb.* metrics. :rocket:
olivia: One open debate: should circuit-breaker consider cost budget exhaustion as a signal? e.g., when tenant is near quota, prefer cheaper model variant even if SLOs are met. Thoughts?
raj: Yes — treat budget pressure as a weighted signal combined with SLO breaches. We can surface 'budget pressure score' in the decision log.
kevin: Implementation note: runtime will need fast evaluation (O(1) per request) — precompile policies into decision-tables keyed by tenant+route+region. Fallbacks should be atomic.
maria: Action items:
- kevin: prototype DSL -> decision-table export (ETA 3d)
- sophie: API contract for /route/evaluate + sample responses (ETA 2d)
- raj: Console mockups for heatmap + preview mode (ETA 5d)
- olivia: propose default fallback chains per model family (ETA 2d)
- all: sync end of week for integration plan
kevin: noted. If anyone wants to pair on DSL edge cases ping me.
maria: Thanks everyone — this is the core of making SLO-driven routing predictable. We'll keep circuit-breaker semantics explicit and surface sim tools in Console.
kevin: 👍
